item.title: Major makeover at Kew's Palm House: moving over 1,300 rare tropical plants 邱园棕榈温室启动大规模翻修：1300 多株珍稀热带植物大迁移
item.description:
本集内容

Major makeover at Kew's Palm House: moving over 1,300 rare tropical plants

邱园棕榈温室启动大规模翻修：1300 多株珍稀热带植物大迁移

文字稿

Rebecca Morelle, BBC correspondent
"This is the world-famous Palm House at Kew Gardens. It's more than 175 years old, and it's about to undergo a makeover on a massive scale. What happens to all of these plants here? There's more than 1,300 of them."

瑞贝卡·莫瑞尔    BBC 通讯员
“这里是世界闻名的邱园棕榈温室（Palm House）。这座温室已有超过 175 年的历史，如今即将迎来一次大规模翻修。温室里的这些植物将去向何方呢？这里生长着 1300 多株植物。”

This marvel of Victorian engineering is home to a tropical treasure trove, but it's posing a horticultural headache.

这座维多利亚时代工程技术的杰作，也是众多珍稀热带植物的宝库，如今却给园艺专家们带来了棘手的园艺难题。

Rebecca Morelle, BBC correspondent
“Every pane of glass needs to be removed and replaced, and the rusting metalwork treated and repainted. But to do that, all of these plants need to be taken out.”

瑞贝卡·莫瑞尔     BBC 通讯员
“温室的每一块玻璃都需要拆除更换，已经生锈的金属结构也要经过除锈和重新喷漆处理。但要完成这些工程，就必须先把这里的所有植物搬出去。”

Tom Pickering, Head of Glasshouse, Royal Botanic Gardens Kew
"It's a really daunting task emptying the collections from the Palm House. Some of them are historically really significant some are actually older than the glass house itself, while other plants are really important conservation species."

汤姆·皮克林    英国皇家植物园邱园温室负责人
“将棕榈温室里的植物全部迁出是一项极其艰巨的任务。其中一些植物具有非常重要的历史价值，甚至比这座玻璃温室本身的历史还要悠久；而另一些则是具有重要保护价值的物种。”

With the plants potted, it's taken on a short journey to its new home.

这些植物被移入花盆后，便踏上了一段前往新 “家” 的短途旅程。

Rebecca Morelle, BBC correspondent
“This is the temporary glass house where all of the larger species are being stored, and it's where they'll stay for at least the next three years while the work here is being done.”

瑞贝卡·莫瑞尔    BBC 通讯员
“这里是一座临时温室，所有体型较大的植物目前都被安置在这里。在翻修工程进行期间，它们将在这里度过至少三年时间。”

It's a carefully controlled environment. Plants need to stay healthy but not grow too big.

这里的环境受到严格控制。工作人员既要确保植物保持健康生长，又不能让它们长得过于高大。

Rebecca Morelle, BBC correspondent
“We've come behind the scenes to the propagation glass house where the team are growing backups of all the plants, in case any of them don't survive the move, there's a botanical plan B.”

瑞贝卡·莫瑞尔    BBC 通讯员
“我们来到了一处平时不对外开放的育苗温室。这里的工作人员正在为棕榈温室里的所有植物培育备份植株。一旦有植物在搬迁过程中无法存活，植物学家们还有备用方案。”

The extinct Myanmar tree is just one of more than 1,000 plants to deal with. It's a huge task, and some of the species are proving a real challenge.

这种在野外已经灭绝的缅甸树种，只是这一千多种待迁移植物中的一种。整个任务规模庞大，而其中一些植物给团队带来了不小的挑战。

Anja Seymour, Botanical horticulturist, Royal Botanic Gardens Kew
"This is ebony, which is a hardwood tropical species. Typically you would propagate it through seed, but unfortunately our specimen doesn't ever flower and then fruit. We've done over 100 cuttings of this one individual, and all but this one haven't succeeded. So this is our little success story. "

安雅·西摩    英国皇家植物园邱园园艺师
“这是乌木，一种热带硬木树种。通常情况下，人们会通过种子来繁殖它，但遗憾的是，我们收藏的这株乌木从未开花结果。我们曾从这棵树上剪取了100多份插穗进行扦插繁殖，但除了眼前这一株，其余都没有成功。所以，它算得上是我们的一个小小成功案例。”

Rebecca Morelle, BBC correspondent
“It's already starting to look pretty sparse in here, but the pressure really is on because in the next six months, everything that's left is going to have to be removed. And not long after that, the work will begin to restore this Palm House to its former glory.”

瑞贝卡·莫瑞尔   BBC 通讯员
“这里看起来已经空旷了不少，但这个任务仍充满压力和挑战。因为在接下来的六个月里，必须把剩余的所有植物全部搬出去。在那之后不久，棕榈温室的修复工程就将启动，让这座历史建筑重现昔日风采。”

重点词汇或表达

makeover 翻新，改造

tropical 热带的

horticultural 园艺的，园艺学的

daunting 艰巨的，令人生畏的

propagate 繁殖，繁育

item.title: Fear for species as world's largest penguin colony loses half a million birds 世界最大企鹅群落减少 50 万只，帽带企鹅前景堪忧
item.description:
本集内容

Fear for species as world's largest penguin colony loses half a million birds

世界最大企鹅群落减少 50 万只，帽带企鹅前景堪忧

文字稿

The world's largest penguin colony has lost its accolade.

世界最大的企鹅群落已经失去了 “最大” 这一头衔。

Zavodovski – a remote volcanic island near Antarctica has lost more than half a million chinstrap penguins since 2011. That's over a quarter of all penguins on the island.

扎瓦多夫斯基岛是南极洲附近的一座偏远火山岛，自 2011 以来，岛上的帽带企鹅已减少超过 50 万只。这相当于全岛企鹅总数的四分之一以上。

Scientists say their food supply's been disrupted by climate-driven changes in the Southern Ocean.

科学家表示，由气候变化引发的南冰洋环境变化扰乱了这些企鹅的食物来源。

Macaroni penguins also live in the region. Their numbers have increased and stabilised on Zavodovski.

马卡罗尼企鹅也生活在这一地区。在扎瓦多夫斯基岛上，它们的数量有所增长并趋于稳定。

They have a broader diet and have been foraging in an area with warmer waters, likely finding alternative foods.

这种企鹅的食物种类更丰富，并在水温较高的海域觅食，很可能因此找到了替代食物。

But as for chinstrap penguins, there's concern their decline on the island and elsewhere could tip them into becoming an endangered species.

但对于帽带企鹅而言，人们担心它们在这座岛上和其它地区的数量持续下降，可能会将这一物种推向濒危状态。

重点词汇或表达

colony  群落，聚居地

volcanic island  火山岛，由火山活动形成的岛屿

climate-driven  气候驱动的，受气候影响的

forage  觅食

tip… into…  使…陷入，把…推向（不利的境地）

item.title: How deep into the Earth have we gone? 人类抵达过地球内部多深的地方？
item.description:
本集内容

How deep into the Earth have we gone?

人类抵达过地球内部多深的地方？

文字稿

What's the deepest into the Earth a human has ever been?

人类曾抵达过地球内部多深的地方？

The answer is only a tiny fraction.

答案是：只进入了极小的一部分。

The outer layer of the Earth is up to 70 kilometres deep in places.

地壳在一些地方厚达 70 公里。

But the deepest a human has ever been is just 4km.

但人类曾抵达过的最深处仅约 4 公里。

That's at a mine in South Africa.

那是在南非的一座矿井中。

We've also tried drilling boreholes, but the deepest one only got about 12km down – just a third of the way through the crust at that point.

人类还尝试过钻探深井，但最深的钻孔也只达到约 12 公里，仅相当于当地地壳厚度的三分之一。

Getting any further is really hard because of the vast pressures and really high temperatures the deeper you go.

想要再往下钻探就变得极其困难，因为越往深处，压力越大、温度越高。

But we can use seismometers to model the layers of the Earth.

不过，我们可以用地震仪来研究地球内部的分层结构。

Seismic waves travel through different materials differently, giving us an idea of what's there even if we can't see it for ourselves.

地震波在不同物质中的传播方式不同，这让我们知道地下深处有什么，即使无法亲眼看到。

This helps us answer questions like why volcanoes erupt, or why earthquakes happen.

这些知识能帮助我们解释一些问题，比如火山为什么会喷发，以及地震为什么会发生。

It can also show us how the Earth has evolved over time, which could help us learn about other planets, too.

它还能让我们了解地球的演变过程，这可能有助于我们研究其他行星。

重点词汇或表达

tiny fraction 极小的一部分

borehole 钻孔

crust 地壳

seismometer 地震仪

model 建立…的模型

item.title: Scottish wildcats: From the brink of extinction to wild-born kittens 苏格兰野猫：从濒临灭绝到野外诞下幼崽
item.description:
本集内容

Scottish wildcats: From the brink of extinction to wild-born kittens

苏格兰野猫：从濒临灭绝到野外诞下幼崽

文字稿

This might look like a tabby, but it is in fact a critically endangered Scottish wildcat. And here in the Highlands, they've been breeding them for release into the wild.

这也许看上去是一只虎斑猫，但它其实是一只极度濒危的苏格兰野猫。在苏格兰高地，人们一直在繁育这些野猫，为的是将它们放归野外。

The cats are closely monitored, have minimal contact with humans.

这些野猫受到严密监测，与人类的接触极少。

Estelle Morgan, Saving Wildcats, Animal Team Leader
"Luckily, the cats are not aware that we're watching them all the time. But yeah, it is a bit like Big Brother for cats."

埃斯特尔·摩根    “拯救野猫” 项目动物团队负责人
“好在这些野猫并不知道我们一直在观察它们。不过，这确实有点像一档野猫版 ‘老大哥’ 节目。”

72 cameras keeping an eye on them day and night.

72 台摄像机日夜监视着野猫们的一举一动。

Estelle Morgan, Saving Wildcats, Animal Team Leader
"We want to know what are the cats actually doing? What are they actually like without us there? Are they able to climb? Are they able to pounce? Can they, you know, navigate complex structures? Are they active at, you know, natural times? What we want to do is ensure that we're releasing cats to the wild that are healthy and that have got the behavioural potential to go and survive in the wild."

埃斯特尔·摩根    “拯救野猫” 项目动物团队负责人
“我们想知道的是，这些野猫到底在做些什么？我们不在场的时候，它们究竟是什么样的？它们能攀爬吗？能猛扑吗？能在复杂的环境中穿行吗？它们会按照符合天性的作息时间活动吗？我们希望确保放归野外的野猫身体健康，同时具备在野外环境中生存所需的行为能力。”

Lorna Gordon, BBC correspondent
"The cats that have been released have established new territories here in the Cairngorms, and the plan now is to go further."

洛娜·戈登    BBC 通讯员
“被放归的野猫已经在凯恩戈姆山脉建立了新领地。现在，项目还计划进一步扩大规模。”

46 have now been released to fend for themselves, and there have been wild-born kittens.

目前已有 46 只野猫被放归野外独立生存，而且已经有在野外出生的幼崽出现。

The population is small but growing.

种群数量虽然不大，但正在增长。

Dr Martin Gaywood, NatureScot
"We've had an enormous amount of success here. It's only the first step. In order to restore the wildcats to the whole of Scotland, we need to plan long-term and we need to plan at a big scale."

马丁·盖伍德博士    苏格兰自然署
“我们在这里取得了巨大的成功。但这只是计划的第一步。为了让野猫能重新回到苏格兰各地，我们需要制定长期、大规模的计划。”

Road traffic, disease and interbreeding all have the potential to impact numbers, as does climate change.

道路交通、疾病和杂交繁殖都可能影响种群数量，气候变化也是如此。

Dr Helen Senn, The Royal Zoological Society of Scotland
"You know, we've had some really big climate incidents here in the Strath over the last couple of years. We've had some major storms and flooding incidents. We've also had, unfortunately, a very significant forest fire in the north of the release area, and all of these things have the potential to impact the population."

海伦·赛恩博士    苏格兰皇家动物学会
“过去几年，这片河谷地区经历了一些非常严重的气候事件。这里曾遭遇强烈的风暴和洪灾。此外，不幸的是，放归区域北部还发生过一场非常严重的森林火灾。所有这些情况都可能对野猫种群造成影响。”

Once released, a close eye is kept on the wildcats now roaming the Cairngorms, a tracker on a collar which will eventually drop off, sending back information.

放归野外后，人们依然会对出没于凯恩戈姆山脉的野猫进行密切监测。它们戴有最终会自然脱落的项圈，上面装有追踪装置，会不断传回信息。

Louise Hughes, Saving Wildcats, Field Operations Manager
"When we're driving around, the receiver is emitting, like, white noise, and then within that white noise, what we're looking for is a very distinctive ping every two seconds."

路易斯·休斯    “拯救野猫” 项目外勤工作负责人
“我们开车巡逻的时候，这个接收器会发出白噪音。我们需要在这片白噪音里捕捉一种很容易辨认的提示音，这种声响每两秒一次。”

Lorna Gordon, BBC correspondent
"Is this it, beeping now?"

洛娜·戈登    BBC 通讯员
“就是这个正在响的哔哔声吗？”

Louise Hughes, Saving Wildcats, Field Operations Manager
"Yeah. That is the signal coming from the collar to tell me that the cat is in the vicinity. To be able to get this amount of information is vitally important to what we're doing, but also the bigger picture of, like, the long-term success of wildcats in the wild."

路易斯·休斯    “拯救野猫” 项目外勤工作负责人
“是的。这就是项圈发出的信号，它告诉我这只野猫就在附近。能获得这么多的信息对我们的工作至关重要，对野猫种群在野外长期生存这一大局也同样重要。”

The hope is that this precious and elusive species of cat will, with a little help, make its home not just here in the Cairngorms, but throughout Scotland once again.

希望在人们的一点帮助下，这种珍稀而行踪隐秘的猫科动物不仅能在凯恩戈姆山脉安家落户，也能重新遍布整个苏格兰。

重点词汇或表达

the Highlands 苏格兰高地

pounce 猛扑；突然扑向（猎物等）

territory 领地，地盘

fend for oneself 独立生存，自力更生

elusive 行踪隐秘的，难以捉摸的

item.title: Could alien life make us sick? 外星生命有可能让人类生病吗？
item.description:
本集内容 

Could alien life make us sick?

外星生命有可能让人类生病吗？

文字稿

If we ever discover alien life in the form of microbes, could they make us sick?

如果我们有一天发现了以微生物形式存在的外星生命，它们会不会使我们生病呢？

Scientists have previously said the chances of Martian surface samples containing biohazards are extremely low.

科学家此前曾表示，火星表面样本中含有生物危害物的可能性极低。

But it's still something they're preparing for.

不过，这仍然是他们正在提前防范的问题之一。

If we ever brought samples back from Mars, they'd be sterilised and contained to make sure they didn't contaminate the Earth.

如果我们将来把火星样本带回地球，样本会经过灭菌并被严格封存，以确保不会污染地球。

But it's not only this so-called backwards contamination we need to think about.

但我们需要考虑的不仅仅是这种所谓的 “反向污染”。

Experts are also questioning what we're taking into space.

专家们也在思考人类究竟把什么带进了太空。

There's evidence that dormant viruses such as the one that causes shingles can become reactivated in space.

有证据表明，一些处于休眠状态的病毒，例如引发带状疱疹的病毒，在太空环境中可能被重新激活。

Studies have suggested astronauts' immune systems could be compromised by spaceflight, so they could be more likely to get sick.

有研究指出，宇航员的免疫系统可能会受到太空飞行的影响而减弱，使他们更容易生病。

And bringing microbes into space could contaminate the very thing we're trying to study.

而且，携带微生物进入太空，可能会污染我们真正想要研究的对象。

We might one day think we've found alien life, but it could actually be microbes we've brought there ourselves.

也许有一天，我们以为自己发现了外星生命，但实际上，那些微生物可能是我们自己从地球带过去的。

Because of this, experts are doing everything they can like sterilising spacecraft to stop microbes hitching a ride.

因此，专家们正在想尽一切办法，比如给航天器消毒，以防微生物 “搭便车”。

重点词汇或表达

microbes 微生物

biohazards 生物危害物

sterilised 灭菌，消毒灭菌

dormant 休眠的，处于休眠状态的

immune systems 免疫系统

item.title: The science behind what stress does to your skin 压力如何影响皮肤？了解其背后的科学原理
item.description:
本集内容

The science behind what stress does to your skin

压力如何影响皮肤？了解其背后的科学原理

文字稿

Stress activates the amygdala – a part of the brain involved in primitive emotions.

压力会激活杏仁体，这是大脑中负责处理本能情绪的相关区域之一。

This signals to a command centre called the hypothalamus, which triggers glands to make various hormones like cortisol and adrenaline.

杏仁体会向被称为身体 “控制中心” 的下丘脑发送信号，后者随即刺激腺体分泌多种激素，比如皮质醇和肾上腺素。

These travel in the bloodstream all over the body, including to your skin.

这些激素会通过血液流经你的全身，包括皮肤。

As well as receiving hormones from the brain's stress response, the skin releases its own stress chemicals too.

除了接收大脑压力反应产生的激素外，皮肤自身也会释放压力化学物质。

Dr Alia Ahmed, consultant dermatologist
"The skin will talk to your brain, and your brain will talk to your skin."

艾莉娅·艾哈迈德医生    皮肤科顾问医师
“皮肤会向大脑传递信息，大脑也会向皮肤传递信息。”

The stress chemicals can boost inflammation, and reduce the fatty lipids that make up the outer skin barrier.

这些压力化学物质可能会加剧炎症反应，并减少构成皮肤屏障外层的脂质成分。

Dr Alia Ahmed, consultant dermatologist
"What we tend to lose from the skin barrier is important things like water. We also can become more sensitive to things in the outside environment. So, for example, allergens like pollen or someone else's fragrance get into the skin and cause irritation."

艾莉娅·艾哈迈德医生    皮肤科顾问医师
“皮肤屏障受损时，我们容易流失一些重要物质，比如水分。我们也会变得对外界环境更加敏感。比如花粉，或他人香水中的香料等过敏原，更容易进入皮肤并引发刺激。”

Stress also activates cells within the skin to release chemicals like histamine that make you feel itchy.

压力还会激活皮肤内部的细胞，让它们释放出组胺等化学物质，从而使你感到瘙痒。

At the same time, stress reduces antimicrobial peptides in the skin, small molecules that normally kill off germs, making infections like cold sores or shingles more likely.

与此同时，压力会减少皮肤中的抗菌肽，这类小分子物质原本能够杀灭病菌，因此会增加唇疱疹和带状疱疹发生的风险。

What's more, the stress chemicals are thought to stimulate glands in the skin to make more of an oily substance called sebum, which can contribute to spots.

此外，也有研究人员认为压力化学物质会刺激皮肤腺体分泌更多皮脂，这是一种油性物质，可能促进粉刺形成。

This might be one of the reasons why people with more stress also tend to have worse acne in various studies.

这或许也是为何许多研究发现压力较大的人痤疮往往更严重的原因之一。

Stress can trigger flare-ups in other skin conditions like eczema, psoriasis and hives too.

压力还可能诱发湿疹、银屑病和荨麻疹等皮肤病的发作。

重点词汇或表达

fatty lipids 脂质

sebum 皮脂

eczema 湿疹

psoriasis 银屑病，牛皮癣

hives 荨麻疹

item.title: What can the male fly brain tell us about the human mind 雄性果蝇的大脑能揭示哪些关于人类思维的奥秘
item.description:
本集内容

What can the male fly brain tell us about the human mind

雄性果蝇的大脑能揭示哪些关于人类思维的奥秘

文字稿

It's as beautiful as it is incredible.

它既美丽，又令人难以置信。

This is the brain and nervous system of a male fly.

这是雄性果蝇的大脑和神经系统。

Every nerve cell sliced up and analysed under an electron microscope and then put together into a 3D map. Two years ago, the same team produced a female fly brain.

每一个神经细胞都被切成薄片，在电子显微镜下进行分析，然后再将这些数据整合起来，构建出一幅三维图谱。两年前，同一研究团队还绘制出了雌性果蝇的大脑图谱。

Dr Isabella Beckett, researcher, Medical Research Council Laboratory of Molecular Biology
"We were expecting to find some differences, and we did find them, and we were really excited by what we got. So in the male fly brain, approximately 5% of what we found was different from the female fly brain. "

伊莎贝拉·贝克特博士    英国医学研究理事会分子生物学实验室研究员
“我们原本预计会发现一些差异，而事实也确实如此，我们对这些发现感到非常兴奋。在雄性果蝇的大脑中，我们发现大约有 5% 的结构与雌性果蝇的大脑不同。”

On the face of it, the male and female brain are pretty similar, but let's take a deep dive inside to find out how tiny changes in wiring can make a big difference to behaviour, such as courtship. The male is in the middle, tracking the female, and these are the bits of wiring involved. The dangly bits enhance the male's visual system.

从表面看，雄性和雌性的果蝇大脑非常相似，但让我们深入大脑内部看看神经连接中的细微变化是如何对行为产生巨大影响的，比如求偶行为。中间的是雄性果蝇，它正在追踪雌性果蝇，而这些就是参与这一过程的神经连接。那些下垂的神经结构能够增强雄性果蝇的视觉系统。

And then there's aggression. Males tend to fight more, and these extra bits here help the male work out when competition is near. And then there's the love song. Males make this sound in order to attract females by beating their wings, and these are the bits that are involved. Now, scientists have known that all three behaviours have been linked to just two genes.

接下来是攻击行为。雄性果蝇往往更具攻击性，而这里这些额外的神经结构能够帮助它们判断附近是否存在竞争对手。然后是 “求爱之歌”。雄性果蝇会通过震动翅膀发出这种声音，以吸引雌性，而这些就是参与这一行为的神经结构。科学家们早已知道，这三种行为都与仅仅两个基因有关。

What they've lacked until now are the bits in the middle. Now, that's important because by being able to link the genes to the wiring to the behaviours in fruit flies, they'll be able to do the same with the brains of other animals, including us.

一直以来，他们所缺少的是连接两者的中间环节。而这一点非常重要，因为一旦能够把果蝇的基因、神经连接和行为联系起来，科学家们就能够用同样的方法研究其它动物的大脑，包括人类的大脑。

Dr Greg Jefferis, Lead researcher, Medical Research Council Laboratory of Molecular Biology
"What we're really trying to do is to understand the anatomy of thought, and we think that the technology we've been using and the logic of linking genes, circuits, and behaviour is going to transfer to other species, you know, and eventually even to humans, where we know, for example, that schizophrenia and autism have very strong genetic components. "

格雷戈里·杰弗里斯博士    英国医学研究理事会分子生物学实验室研究负责人
“我们真正想做的是理解 ‘思维的解剖结构’，我们认为，我们一直使用的技术，以及将基因、神经回路和行为联系起来的研究思路，也可以应用到其它物种身上，并最终应用于人类。例如，我们知道精神分裂症和自闭症都具有很强的遗传因素。”

The fly brain maps are the first step in truly understanding not just how their brains work, but ours too.

果蝇大脑图谱只是第一步，它将帮助我们真正理解大脑是如何运作的，不仅是果蝇的大脑，也包括人类的大脑。

重点词汇或表达

take a deep dive 深入研究

enhance 增强，提高，改善

anatomy 解剖结构

autism 自闭症

genetic 遗传的，与遗传有关的

item.title: How going slow can increase your enjoyment of art 慢下来欣赏艺术，为何能让你获得更多乐趣
item.description:
本集内容

How going slow can increase your enjoyment of art

慢下来欣赏艺术，为何能让你获得更多乐趣

文字稿

How long do you spend looking at art?

你会花多长时间欣赏一件艺术品？

Studies suggest we tend to view a single piece for just 10 seconds.

研究表明，我们欣赏一件艺术品的时间往往只有 10 秒钟。

If you race around a gallery, you see lots more paintings and sculptures of course, but some experts think we're losing an opportunity.

如果你匆匆逛完一座美术馆，当然能看到更多绘画和雕塑，但一些专家认为，我们也因此错失了更深入欣赏艺术的机会。

Jake Blackavar, Visitor Experience and Engagement Facilitator, Wellcome Collection
"You won't remember it all. You're missing out on building a relationship with two or three works of art. It's feeding into this rushed lifestyle."

杰克·布莱卡瓦 惠康收藏馆参观体验与互动专员
“这样你不可能记住所有看过的作品。也错过了与其中两三件作品建立真正联系的机会。这种做法还会进一步助长快节奏、匆匆忙忙的生活方式。”

Now, people are promoting the concept of Slow Art. The idea is to push back against the fast pace of modern life by looking at fewer pieces of art for longer.

如今，人们正在推广 “慢艺术” 这一理念。“慢艺术” 提倡人们用更长时间去欣赏更少的艺术品，以此来对抗现代生活的快节奏。

Jake Blackavar, Visitor Experience and Engagement Facilitator, Wellcome Collection
"Choose a work of art that interests you and don't read the label. Set a timer between five and 10 minutes. Examine where your thoughts go. Follow any emotions or feelings or memories that arise while you're looking at the work."

杰克·布莱卡瓦 惠康收藏馆参观体验与互动专员
“选择一件你感兴趣的艺术作品，先不要阅读旁边的说明文字。设定一个五到 10 分钟的计时器，留意自己的思绪会飘向何处，并感受在欣赏过程中浮现出的情绪、感情或回忆。”

Jake Blackavar, Visitor Experience and Engagement Facilitator, Wellcome Collection
"See if there's any sensory elements to it, if it has texture or smells or tastes. And then it might help you if you jot thoughts down, use a clipboard or your phone, just to write thoughts down as you go. And then when the timer goes off, you're allowed to look at the label and see if it matches your interpretations, or if you came up with something completely different."

杰克·布莱卡瓦 惠康收藏馆参观体验与互动专员
“看看这件作品是否具有某种感官层面的元素，比如质感、气味或味道。然后，随手记下自己的想法或许会有所帮助，可以用带夹子的写字板，也可以用手机，在欣赏过程中随时记下脑海中浮现出的想法。等计时器响起后，你就可以去阅读作品说明，看看它是否与你的解读相符，还是你产生了完全不同的理解。”

Research shows looking for longer produces deeper emotional responses.

研究发现，花更长时间欣赏艺术作品，往往能激发更深层的情感反应。

重点词汇或表达

missing out 错过，错失

feeding into 助长，促成

promote 促进，提倡

push back 反对，抵制

interpretation 理解，解读

item.title: Why can we be so scared of things that probably won't hurt us? 为什么我们会害怕那些其实不会伤害我们的东西？
item.description:
本集内容

Why can we be so scared of things that probably won't hurt us?

为什么我们会害怕那些其实不会伤害我们的东西？

文字稿

Most spiders and snakes aren't likely to hurt us, so why are we so scared of them?

大多数蜘蛛和蛇其实都不太可能会伤害我们，那么我们为什么会如此害怕它们呢？

Scientists generally think emotions like fear are not innate.

科学家普遍认为，恐惧等情绪并非与生俱来。

Professor Vanessa LoBue, psychologist, Rutgers University
"They're not there at birth and you need cognition and experience in order to feel them."

瓦妮莎·洛布教授    罗格斯大学心理学教授
“这些情绪并非与生俱来，而是需要通过认知和经验才会逐渐产生。”

But we might be predisposed to learn to fear certain things.

但我们可能天生更容易学会害怕某些事物。

In one study, infants' pupils dilated more when looking at spiders or snakes compared with flowers and fish – a sign they might be perceiving potential danger.

在一项研究中，婴儿的瞳孔在看到蜘蛛或蛇时，比看到花朵和鱼类扩张得更明显——这表明他们可能察觉到了潜在的危险。

From there, a phobia might develop in a few ways.

在此基础上，恐惧症可能通过几种方式形成。

Professor Vanessa LoBue, psychologist, Rutgers University
"One is we experience a negative response right away. So, a lot of kids are afraid of dogs because dogs either have barked at them, have bit them. And then there's the other two that are more common, which is watching someone else be afraid. So there's a spider on the wall, and the mum [gasps]. The other is by verbal information and a lot of fears are learned this way. Think about media, books, what people say."

瓦妮莎·洛布教授    罗格斯大学心理学教授
“其中一种情况是，我们直接就经历了一次负面的体验。比如，很多孩子会害怕狗，因为狗曾对他们狂吠，甚至咬过他们。另外还有两种更常见的方式。其中一种是看到他人感到害怕。比如墙上有只蜘蛛，妈妈 ‘啊’ 的一声叫出来……另一种则是通过语言信息获得。很多恐惧都是这样习得的，比如来自媒体、书籍以及人们所说的话。”

But our phobias don't have to be there for life.

但我们的恐惧并不一定要伴随我们一生。

Professor Vanessa LoBue, psychologist, Rutgers University
“Exposure therapy is, I think, the best way. Just start with really, really benign photos of something and look at positive facts about them, then getting closer and closer to that object is helpful. if you're afraid of something and you don't want to be, there are solutions.”

瓦妮莎·洛布教授    罗格斯大学心理学教授
“我认为暴露疗法是克服恐惧最好的方法。可以先从那些不会引起太大不适的照片开始，再去了解关于它的积极信息，然后逐渐靠近那个对象很有帮助。如果你害怕某样东西，而且不想一直这样下去，有一些方法能帮到你。”

重点词汇或表达

innate 与生俱来的

cognition 认知，认知能力

predisposed 天生更容易…的，预先有倾向的

perceive 感知，察觉

phobia 恐惧，恐惧症

item.title: 97-year-old woman breaks another wingwalking record a year after stroke 97 岁老妇人在中风一年后再次打破 “机翼行走” 世界纪录
item.description:
本集内容

97-year-old woman breaks another wingwalking record a year after stroke

97 岁老妇人在中风一年后再次打破 “机翼行走” 世界纪录

文字稿

A 97-year-old woman, who suffered a stroke in 2025, has broken the Guinness World Record for being the oldest female wingwalker.

一名曾于 2025 年中风的 97 岁女性打破了吉尼斯世界纪录，成为全球年龄最大的女性 “机翼行走者”。

Betty Bromage, who lives in Cheltenham, broke her own record which was set when she did the same challenge four years ago.

居住在切尔滕纳姆的贝蒂·布罗马奇打破了自己四年前在同一挑战中创下的世界纪录。

By accomplishing this challenging stunt, Bromage raised funds for the stroke unit at Cheltenham General Hospital, where staff cared for her when she was sick.

通过完成这项极具挑战性的特技表演，布罗马奇为切尔滕纳姆总医院的卒中病房筹集了善款。她中风住院时，那里的医护人员曾为她提供悉心照顾。

Betty Bromage, world-record-breaking wingwalker
"I'd just get bored at life otherwise. When you get old you can't go here, you can't do this, you can't drive, you can't see. I can't see very well, and I get a bit frustrated. So I want to do the things that I can do."

贝蒂·布罗马奇    打破世界纪录的 “机翼行走者”
“如果不去挑战，我可能就要对生活感到厌倦了。人老了以后，这也不能去，那也不能做，开不了车，也看不清东西。我现在的视力就大不如前，这让我有点沮丧。所以我想去做那些自己还能做到的事情。”

Last year, she had a stroke which still affects her speech, but she says that otherwise her health is good.

去年，她经历了一次中风，至今说话仍受到一定影响。但她说自己其它方面的身体状况还不错。

While she was taking on the wingwalking challenge again, her friends and neighbours watched nervously and cheered her on.

当她再次挑战 “机翼行走” 时，她的朋友和邻居们紧张地看着她，为她加油鼓劲。

Betty's friend
"Go, Betty!"

贝蒂的朋友
“加油，贝蒂！”

BBC correspondent
"What was it like watching her doing those loop-the-loops in there?"

BBC 通讯员
“看着她在空中完成那些翻筋斗的特技动作，是什么感受？”

Betty's friend
"Awful. I was here four years ago. Awful. Makes you want to cry. But yeah, she got on fantastic. Yeah. So proud of her."

贝蒂的朋友
“太吓人了。我四年前就在这看过一次，把我吓坏了。真的让人想哭。不过，她表现得太棒了。我真为她感到骄傲。”

重点词汇或表达

stroke 中风

raised funds 募集善款，募捐

frustrated 沮丧的

cheer… on 为（某人）加油助威

loop-the-loops 翻筋斗式特技飞行动作

item.title: Bumblebees struggling in UK heatwaves 英国熊蜂在热浪中艰难求生
item.description:
本集内容

Bumblebees struggling in UK heatwaves

英国熊蜂在热浪中艰难求生

文字稿

A group of volunteers are meeting in West Wales.

一队志愿者正在威尔士西部聚集。

They are here to learn how to count one of the country's favourite insects, because our bumblebees are in trouble.

他们来到这里学习如何统计熊蜂的数量，因为这种英国最喜爱的昆虫之一正面临危机。

New analysis of data collected by volunteers like these show the impact of the record breaking heatwaves of 2022, when temperatures breached 40 degrees for the first time.

一项针对这些志愿者所收集数据的新分析显示出了 2022 年创纪录热浪造成的影响。当时，英国气温首次突破 40 摄氏度。

The populations of three of the most common UK bumblebees crashed by between 20 and 35 per cent.

英国最常见的三种熊蜂的种群数量锐减了 20% 到 35%。

Dr Richard Comont, Bumblebee Conservation Trust
"If it gets too hot, if the outside air temperature gets much above about 30 degrees, bumblebees really struggle to fly. They actually cook themselves from the inside out. Once their internal body temperature is much above 40, they literally start dying. They start keeling over. They can't survive at that kind of temperature."

里查德·科蒙博士    熊蜂保护信托基金
“如果天气炎热，气温远远超过 30 摄氏度，熊蜂就很难飞行。它们实际上会从身体内部开始过热。一旦体内温度超过 40 度，熊蜂就会开始死亡，它们会接连倒下，无法在这样的高温环境中存活。”

We think of bumblebees as creatures of the summer heat drifting lazily between flowers, but they are actually a temperate species, cleverly adapted to cooler climates. In very hot weather, they have to take shelter.

我们总觉得熊蜂是盛夏时节的生物，在花丛间悠闲地飞来飞去，但实际上它们属于温带物种，已经巧妙地适应了较凉爽的气候。在炎热的天气里，它们也必须寻找庇护之所。

And if they can't fly, they can't forage – can't collect food, making it harder to rear young bumblebees.

如果熊蜂无法飞行，就不能觅食，这会使它们更难养育幼蜂。

The fact that most of the flower-rich meadows in which they used to thrive were cut back decades ago, makes it even more difficult for them.

它们过去赖以繁衍生息的大部分繁花草甸早在数十年前就已经大幅减少，这让它们的处境愈发艰难。

And heat and drought can dry out what flowers are left, leaving bumblebees without food.

高热和干旱还会使所剩无几的花朵枯萎，让熊蜂失去食物来源。

Dr Richard Comont, Bumblebee Conservation Trust
"For a lot of species, it's a real cliff edge, I would say. A lot of them are just about hanging on, and it doesn't take much – one really cold spring, one really hot summer, one field cut at the wrong time of year could be enough just to doom that population. Bumblebees need a big, well-connected area for a population to survive in."

里查德·科蒙博士    熊蜂保护信托基金
“我认为，对于许多物种来说，它们已经处在生存的悬崖边缘。许多物种都只是在勉强维持，而一点点小打击，比如一个异常寒冷的春天、一个异常炎热的夏天，或是一片草地在不合时宜的时候被割除，都足以令一个种群走向灭绝。熊蜂种群要生存下来，需要面积足够大且彼此联通的栖息地。”

But bumblebee populations can be bolstered.

不过，熊蜂种群依然有机会得到恢复。

This farm in West Wales focuses on supporting insects alongside producing food.

这家农场位于威尔士西部，在生产粮食的同时，也致力于为昆虫创造适宜的生存环境。

Dr Sarah Beynon, conservationist
"We're trying to create as much diverse habitat as possible. So right through from this time of year where we've got our meadows flowering, we've got willows that we're planting to provide early nectar and pollen sources for the bumblebees. We've got the tussocky grasses for them to overwinter in and also for, for them to nest build, creating hedge banks for them to build nests in."

莎拉·贝农博士    环境保护人士
“我们正尽可能创造多样化的栖息地。从每年草甸开花的时候开始，我们会种植柳树，为熊蜂提供早期的花蜜和花粉来源。我们会种植丛生草地供它们越冬和筑巢，还修建树篱来为它们提供筑巢场所。”

In a hotter, more volatile climate, the challenge is not just helping bumblebees survive the next heatwave, it's making sure there's enough food in the landscape for them to recover afterwards.

随着气候变得越来越热、越来越不稳定，人们面临的挑战已不仅仅是帮助熊蜂熬过下一波热浪。我们还需要确保它们所处的生态环境中有充足的食物资源，让熊蜂种群在热浪过后得以恢复。

重点词汇或表达

breach 突破，冲破

keeling over 突然倒下

forage 觅食，采集食物

cliff edge 悬崖边缘，危险边缘

hang on 勉强维持，艰难求生
